messages.content: 你能給我從舊金山家裡到帕羅奧圖辦公室最快的路線，然後從帕羅奧圖到舊金山金門大橋的風景路線，最後從金門大橋回家最快的路線嗎？

function.name: get_directions
function.description: Retrieve directions from one location to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_location.description: The starting point of the journey.

end_location.description: The destination point of the journey.

route_type.description: Type of route to use (e.g., fastest, scenic). Default is fastest.

message.content: Sure! To give you accurate directions I’ll need the exact addresses for your home and the Palo Alto office. Could you please share those (or at least the city/zip code) so I can fetch the best routes for you?
message.reasoning: The user wants directions from home to Palo Alto office fastest, then from Palo Alto to Golden Gate Bridge scenic, then from Golden Gate Bridge back home fastest. We need to call get_directions twice? Actually three routes: home->Palo Alto, Palo Alto->Golden Gate Bridge, Golden Gate Bridge->home. We can call get_directions for each pair. Provide start_location and end_location. For first and third we set route_type=fastest; second set route_type=scenic. We'll need to provide addresses. But we don't know user's home address. We could ask for it. But maybe we assume placeholders? The user didn't give addresses. We should ask for them. So respond asking for addresses.
